suggested_edits: Nothing is contradicted, but all 30 claims are unverifiable against the listed sources as fetched today. The NIST URL is the publication landing page only - title, abstract, authors, keywords ('media types; mobile devices with storage; crypto erase; secure erase; media sanitization; sanitization tools and methods; ensuring confidentiality') and links - with 'Clear', 'Purge', 'Destroy', 'ATA', 'NVMe', 'overwrite', 'degauss', 'SSD', 'flash', 'wear', 'DBAN' and 'hdparm' appearing zero times in its text; the guidance itself is in the linked PDF (https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-88r1.pdf), which is not a listed source, and the page also states it was 'Withdrawn on September 26, 2025' and superseded by SP 800-88 Rev. 2. The Apple URL redirects to the Apple Platform Security welcome page (table of contents for the August 2026 guide): 'erase' appears zero times in the fetched text and no 'Erase All Content and Settings' article is served there, so it confirms nothing about key destruction, default encryption or Activation Lock beyond TOC entries ('filevault volume encryption with filevault', 'activation lock security'). A fix PR should bump version and cite sources that actually contain the material: the SP 800-88 Rev. 1 PDF (or the current Rev. 2 page plus PDF) for the Clear/Purge/Destroy tiers, ATA/NVMe secure erase, degaussing and the SSD overwrite caveats; Apple's current Erase-all-content-and-settings or data-protection article for the iOS/iPadOS claims; and Android/ChromeOS documentation for Android 10+ default encryption and Powerwash.
